new.title: Walk the world's longest castle in Burghausen
new.desc: Burg Burghausen stretches about 1,050 m along a ridge above the Salzach and the Wöhrsee, and is recognised as the longest castle complex in the world. Six courtyards lead from the outer gate to the Hauptburg, which holds the museum.
new.tip: The castle grounds are open all day and free; only the museums charge a few euros. Allow two hours and walk the full length.

new.title: Visit the Black Madonna in Altötting's Gnadenkapelle
new.desc: The octagonal Gnadenkapelle on the Kapellplatz is Bavaria's national shrine. It holds the roughly 70 cm Gothic lime-wood Madonna, blackened by candle soot, which draws over a million pilgrims a year.
new.tip: Open daily from early morning until evening and free to enter. Go early to avoid the pilgrim crowds.

new.title: Tour the baroque library of Metten Abbey
new.desc: Metten Abbey was founded in 766, dissolved in 1803 and re-established in 1830. Its baroque library, with atlas figures carrying the vaults, holds about 35,000 works and can only be seen on a guided tour.
new.tip: Tours run at set times, usually twice a day; check kloster-metten.de first. Tickets cost a few euros.

new.title: See the abbey basilica at Niederalteich on the Danube
new.desc: Niederaltaich Abbey was founded in 741 and is one of the oldest Bavarian monasteries. The basilica of St Mauritius and St Nikolaus is a Benedictine church, and the abbey has a living link to Byzantine-rite Christianity through its ecumenical work.
new.tip: The basilica is open in daytime and the abbey offers guided tours. Combine with a stretch of the Danube cycle path.

new.title: Walk the treetop path above the Bavarian Forest
new.desc: The Baumwipfelpfad at Neuschönau is a barrier-free walkway through the canopy of the Bavarian Forest National Park, ending at a tower with views over the forest towards the Lusen.
new.tip: Open all year, last entry an hour before closing; closed in storms and ice. Dogs are not allowed. Check treetop-walks.com for current prices.

new.title: Spot wolves and lynx at the Tierfreigelände Neuschönau
new.desc: This large open-air animal park of the Bavarian Forest National Park shows about 40 native species such as wolf, lynx, brown bear, otter and eagle owl in big natural enclosures. The main loop is about 7 km.
new.tip: Entry is free and the park is open all year; plan three to four hours for the full loop or use the shortcuts.

new.title: Explore glass art at the Glasmuseum Frauenau
new.desc: The Glasmuseum Frauenau shows the glass history of the Bavarian Forest, from historic glass to contemporary studio glass, in a park setting. Frauenau is one of the old glassmaking villages of the region.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday, 9:00 to 17:00. Check prices on the museum site.

new.title: Admire the Renaissance courtyard of Schloss Ortenburg
new.desc: Schloss Ortenburg, about 20 km west of Passau, took its present Renaissance form around 1562. It holds a coffered ceiling from 1628 and a museum around a restored courtyard.
new.tip: Visits are by guided tour or museum opening; check times with the castle office before travelling.

new.title: Visit the Danube museum in Schloss Obernzell
new.desc: Schloss Obernzell on the Danube houses the Bayerisches Donauland-Museum, a branch of the Bavarian National Museum that opened in July 2025. The museum began in 1982 as a ceramics museum.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00 to 17:00, with a winter closure from early January to the end of March.

new.title: Stroll the Stadtplatz and Altes Rathaus in Deggendorf
new.desc: The Altes Rathaus of 1535, attached to a Gothic tower from around 1380, divides Deggendorf's long Stadtplatz into two market streets lined with coloured burgher houses.
new.tip: Best on a market day; cafés and restaurants line the square.

new.title: See the Heilig-Grab-Kirche at the end of Deggendorf's square
new.desc: The Heilig-Grab-Kirche St. Peter und St. Paul dates from the 14th century and was built after 1338 on the site of the former synagogue. Its bell tower closes the south end of the Stadtplatz.
new.tip: Open to visitors as a church; read the information on its history and on the former Deggendorfer Gnad pilgrimage.

new.title: Climb to the Gartlberg pilgrimage church in Pfarrkirchen
new.desc: The Wallfahrtskirche zur Schmerzhaften Muttergottes on the Gartlberg was built in the 1660s. It is a double-towered baroque church with onion domes and the best-known landmark of Pfarrkirchen.
new.tip: Combine with the old cemetery and a walk through the town; the church is usually open in daytime.

new.title: Walk Eggenfelden's medieval Stadtplatz
new.desc: Eggenfelden's Stadtplatz is a long street market of the typical Lower Bavarian type, laid out in the early 14th century, with the Marienbrunnen and the Gothic-core Luibl-Haus.
new.tip: Free to wander; the Luiblhaus café on the square is a handy breakfast stop.

new.title: Tour the late-Gothic Herzogsburg in Dingolfing
new.desc: The Herzogsburg in Dingolfing, built between 1410 and 1477, is one of the best-preserved late-Gothic secular buildings in Lower Bavaria. It houses the Museum Dingolfing on town and industrial history, open as a museum since 20 June 1959.
new.tip: Entry to the museum is free; check museum-dingolfing.de for opening times.

new.title: Discover the monastery brewery museum in Aldersbach
new.desc: The Bräuseum in the former monastery brewery at Aldersbach explains Bavarian brewing in an 18th-century brewhouse and cellar building. The Aldersbach brewery itself dates back to the 13th century.
new.tip: Located at Freiherr-von-Aretin-Platz 1; check aldersbacher.de for current times.

new.title: See the border station of Bayerisch Eisenstein
new.desc: The station at Bayerisch Eisenstein sits right on the Czech border and is the end of the Waldbahn line from Plattling via Zwiesel, a gateway between the Bavarian Forest and the Bohemian Forest.
new.tip: Trains run roughly hourly from Zwiesel; check for replacement buses before travelling.
new.q: Bahnhof Bayerisch Eisenstein, Bahnhofstraße 54, 94252 Bayerisch Eisenstein

new.title: Stand on the boulder summit of the Lusen
new.desc: The Lusen, at 1,373 m, is one of the highest peaks of the Bavarian Forest National Park. Its summit is covered in granite boulders and can only be reached on foot, with the Lusenschutzhaus just below it.
new.tip: Avoid the exposed summit in thunderstorms; the hut is open seasonally.
new.q: Lusen Gipfel, Nationalpark Bayerischer Wald, 94556 Neuschönau

new.title: Ride or hike up the Großer Arber
new.desc: At 1,456 m the Großer Arber is the highest mountain of the Bavarian Forest. A gondola runs from Bayerisch Eisenstein to near the summit, and the circuit around the Arbersee takes about 35 minutes.
new.tip: The gondola runs daily in summer; check arber.de for hours and fares. Parking is about 4 EUR per day.

new.title: Hike from Waldhausreibe up to the Lusen
new.desc: The standard route climbs from Waldhausreibe past the Himmelsleiter to the boulder-strewn Lusen summit. The summer path and the winter path past the Lusenschutzhaus both start at the same car park.
new.tip: Wear sturdy boots and bring water; allow about four hours for the loop.

new.title: Hike to Rachelsee and the Großer Rachel summit
new.desc: From the Gfäll car park the Auerhahn trail climbs about 520 m past the Rachelkapelle to the 1,453 m summit of the Großer Rachel. The Rachelsee is the only large natural lake in the national park.
new.tip: The Igelbus runs from Spiegelau to Gfäll from mid-May to the end of October.

new.title: Soak in the thermal waters of Europa Therme, Bad Füssing
new.desc: Bad Füssing is one of Germany's busiest spa towns, and Europa Therme is one of its large thermal baths. Children under three are not admitted.
new.tip: Open daily; check europatherme.de for prices and guest-card discounts.

new.title: Take an evening swim at Therme Eins in Bad Füssing
new.desc: Therme Eins at Kurallee 1 is one of the thermal baths of Bad Füssing, with a sauna area. An evening ticket applies from Wednesday to Sunday after 17:00.
new.tip: The evening ticket was listed at 12 EUR in late 2025; check thermeeins.de.

new.title: Bathe at the Rottal Terme in Bad Birnbach
new.desc: The Rottal Terme is the thermal spa of Bad Birnbach, with indoor and outdoor pools and the Vitarium sauna world. Events include moonlight bathing and sauna nights.
new.tip: Open daily; check badbirnbach.de for hours. Monday evening is ladies' night in the sauna.

new.title: Relax at the Wohlfühl-Therme in Bad Griesbach
new.desc: The Wohlfühl-Therme is a thermal bath in the spa town of Bad Griesbach im Rottal, with a sauna area. It is generally open until 20:00.
new.tip: Check wohlfuehltherme.de for hours and prices; it may close on public holidays.

new.title: Ride the Waldbahn from Zwiesel to Bayerisch Eisenstein
new.desc: The Waldbahn connects Plattling, Zwiesel and Bayerisch Eisenstein, with other branches to Frauenau, Grafenau, Bodenmais and Viechtach. It is an easy way to reach the Arber and the border region without a car.
new.tip: Trains leave Zwiesel at minute 59 towards Bayerisch Eisenstein; check waldbahn.de for disruptions.

new.title: Go underground in the Silberberg mine at Bodenmais
new.desc: The Historisches Besucherbergwerk on the Silberberg takes visitors into the old ore mine at Bodenmais. A cable car also runs up the Silberberg in summer.
new.tip: Mine hours vary by season, roughly 10:00 to 16:00 from spring to October; confirm on the official site.

new.title: Swim in the Wöhrsee beneath Burghausen castle
new.desc: The Wöhrsee lies directly below Burghausen castle and has a lido with a diving tower, slides, paddle boards and boat hire. Walking loops around the lake and over the Wöhrsee bridge give views of the castle.
new.tip: The lido is open May to September, typically 8:00 to 20:00.

new.title: Mint a glass coin at the Eisch glassworks in Frauenau
new.desc: At the Eisch glassworks reception visitors can take part in glass coin minting on Tuesdays to Saturdays at 9:30 and 11:00. The factory outlet also offers wine glass tastings.
new.tip: Meet at reception at Althüttenstraße 30; the coin surcharge was 2.50 EUR. Call ahead for dates.

new.title: Meet the animals at Wildpark Schloss Ortenburg
new.desc: The Wildpark by Schloss Ortenburg is a family animal park open from late March to early November, daily 9:00 to 19:00. A combined ticket with the nearby Tierpark Irgenöd is offered.
new.tip: Last entry about 17:30. In winter it opens only on good-weather weekends.

new.title: Hike the Pfahl ridge to Burgruine Weißenstein
new.desc: Burg Weißenstein is a ruined rock castle at 758 m on the quartz ridge of the Pfahl above Regen. Loop trails of 5 to 13 km lead to it through the Pfahl nature reserve.
new.tip: Check the official Regen page before going, since access to the ruin itself has been reported as restricted.

new.title: Drink Dampfbier at the Schalander of Brauerei Pfeffer, Zwiesel
new.desc: The Dampfbierbrauerei Zwiesel has brewed since 1889 and is known for its amber, top-fermented Dampfbier. Its Schalander restaurant and beer garden adjoins the historic brewery.
new.tip: Order the Dampfbier; the historic brewery and Schalander keep limited weekday afternoon hours, so check first.

new.title: Eat a Brotzeit at Brauerei-Gasthof Eck in Böbrach
new.desc: Brauerei-Gasthof Eck in Böbrach has brewed since 1462 and has a traditional beer garden on a hill outside the village. It also runs a hotel.
new.tip: Warm kitchen is listed from 11:30 to 20:30, Monday closed; try the house beer with a Brotzeit.

new.title: Order the veal sausage breakfast at Altöttinger Hof
new.desc: Gasthof Altöttinger Hof in Altötting is a Bavarian inn with its own butcher shop, a fireplace room and a beer garden. Its veal sausage breakfast is a well-known house offering.
new.tip: Order the veal sausage breakfast.
new.q: Gasthof Altöttinger Hof, Mühldorfer Straße 1, 84503 Altötting

new.title: Have a Wolferstetter beer in the Keller in Vilshofen
new.desc: The Wolferstetter Keller at Bürg 21 in Vilshofen is a traditional Bavarian beer garden with a vaulted restaurant, tied to the local Wolferstetter brewery.
new.tip: Order the Wolferstetter beer with a Bavarian main; call ahead for current hours.
new.q: Wolferstetter Keller, Bürg 21, 94474 Vilshofen an der Donau

new.title: Eat Bavarian-Bohemian dishes at Goldener Engel, Deggendorf
new.desc: The Goldene Engel on Deggendorf's Oberer Stadtplatz is a rustic inn in the historic centre with a Bavarian menu that includes Bohemian influences.
new.tip: Choose a dumpling dish; confirm opening hours before going.

new.title: Dine at Brauereigasthof Falter in Regen
new.desc: Privatbrauerei J.B. Falter in Regen runs the Hotel Brauereigasthof Falter, a brewery inn with its own horse-drawn carriages and Percheron stable.
new.tip: Try the house beer with a regional Bavarian dish.

new.title: Eat in the Klostergasthof Raitenhaslach near Burghausen
new.desc: The Klostergasthof Raitenhaslach is an inn in the converted baroque monastery at Raitenhaslach, near Burghausen.
new.tip: Order Bavarian specialities from the daily menu.

new.title: Eat fresh Spätzle at the Braustüberl of Lang-Bräu, Freyung
new.desc: Lang-Bräu Freyung runs a Braustüberl serving regional food with its own beer. The brewhouse and cellar can be visited on request.
new.tip: Look for the fresh Spätzle dishes and the house beer; call ahead for hours.

new.title: Taste Grafenauer Helles from Bucher Bräu
new.desc: Bucher Bräu in Grafenau is a family brewery in the Bavarian Forest that brews ten beers; its best seller is the Grafenauer Helles.
new.tip: Try the Grafenauer Helles; check the current Gaststätte hours.

new.title: Eat in the beer garden of the Mettner Hof
new.desc: The Mettner Hof in Metten has a beer garden serving Bavarian and international dishes, close to Metten Abbey.
new.tip: Eat in the beer garden after the abbey library tour.

new.title: Try Lidwina Bayer Weisse in Deggendorf
new.desc: The Josef Bayer Weißbierbrauerei is described as the oldest wheat-beer brewery in Deggendorf, with its Bayer-Weizen and Lidwina Bayer Weisse.
new.tip: Taste the Bayer Weizen.
